scenes.caption: Okay, quick game. Myth or fact? Data centres edition.
Hmm, no. That's a myth. Servers turn almost all their power into heat, and many data centres cool down with water. A 2025 study found up to 50 Indian data centres in extremely water-stressed areas.
"Okay, but they use most of the world's electricity, right?"
Not quite. About 1.5% in 2024. But here's the thing: the IEA says it could more than double by 2030.
"Fine. But India's power is mostly clean now."
Half true! Over half of India's power capacity is non-fossil now. But coal still makes most of the electricity we actually use.
So, the good news? The fixes are real. Cleaner power, smarter cooling, less water. We just have to choose them.

sources: Planet Tracker (2025), as reported by Climate Fact Checks: up to 50 Indian data centres in extremely high water-stress regions
IEA, Energy and AI (2025): data centres ~1.5% of global electricity in 2024; ~945 TWh projected by 2030
MNRE: non-fossil sources over 54% of installed capacity (31 July 2026)
